text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein orders that elections be held with utmost impartiality; expectations polling day could be November 4 while interior minister hopes all political trends will take part.
- Royal court chief Awn al-Khasawneh meets Moslem Brotherhood head Abdul Majid Thuneibat to discuss reasons why they decided to boycott coming parliamentary elections.
- Islamic Action Front council expected to decide on Thursday to boycott elections.
- Firefighters put out blaze in "forest of peace" border post area with Israel caused by old minefield.
- Moslem Brotherhood says dialogue with government to start next week; parliament speaker expected to take part.
- King issues decree declaring elections on time; government will hold fair polls, says interior minister.
- Palestinian Airlines' first flight lands in Amman.
